_meta.note: name field is the verbatim injection string. injury key 'Foot / Ankle' matches code spelling.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.cue: Hold weight at chest, push knees out over pinky toes, keep chest tall — heels stay flat the entire set.
exercises.rationale: The counterbalance naturally creates an upright torso — self-correcting for forward lean and the safest entry point for the loaded squat pattern.
exercises.notes: Knee mod: elevate heels on plates. Ankle mod: same.

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.cue: Sit back to the box with control, pause briefly without relaxing, drive through heels to stand — box height sets the range of motion.
exercises.rationale: The box teaches proper squat mechanics by breaking the eccentric-concentric stretch reflex, reduces knee shear force, and is ideal for knee and low back clients.
exercises.notes: Low back mod: higher box. Knee mod: heel elevation + higher box.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Squat
exercises.cue: Stand centered in the bar, push the floor away rather than pulling the bar up, lock hips out completely at the top with a glute squeeze.
exercises.rationale: The trap bar shifts load from the spine to the hips and legs, dramatically reducing lumbar shear — the most spine-friendly barbell squat variation available.
exercises.notes: Best all-around primary squat for general population.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.cue: Bar sits on upper traps, brace hard before unracking, squat to depth with knees tracking toes — do not let lower back round at the bottom.
exercises.rationale: The gold standard bilateral lower body movement for strength and muscle development — high neural demand and full posterior chain engagement.
exercises.notes: Elder contraindicated. Low back: use only with excellent hip mobility.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.cue: Elbows high and forward throughout — if elbows drop the bar comes forward, brace before descent and stay as upright as possible.
exercises.rationale: Front loading forces an upright torso and high core demand — excellent for quad development and Olympic lift preparation.
exercises.notes: Requires significant wrist and shoulder mobility.

exercises.name: Hack Squat Machine
exercises.cue: Place feet shoulder width at mid-platform, lower until thighs are parallel, drive through full foot — do not lock out knees aggressively at the top.
exercises.rationale: Machine stability removes balance demand allowing maximum quad loading — ideal for hypertrophy focus and clients with mobility restrictions.
exercises.notes: Low back mod: reduce range. Knee mod: higher foot placement.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.cue: Feet shoulder width at mid-plate, lower until 90 degrees without lower back rounding off the pad — do not lock knees at the top.
exercises.rationale: Allows heavy quad loading with minimal spinal demand — excellent for Elder avatar, injury protocols, and hypertrophy work when primary squat is loaded heavy.
exercises.notes: Operator and Apex use as accessory not primary.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.cue: Lower straight down — front shin stays vertical and back knee drops directly under the hip — do not lunge forward.
exercises.rationale: Exposes single leg strength asymmetries in a stable environment before loading — essential screening and corrective movement for all avatars.
exercises.notes: Knee mod: shorter stride, reduce range. Low back: brace harder.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Rear foot elevated on bench, lower straight down with control — front shin stays vertical and hip flexor of rear leg stretches fully.
exercises.rationale: Eliminates rear leg assistance creating a true single leg challenge — the highest unilateral strength exercise available for quad and glute development.
exercises.notes: Elder: use only if stable on two feet first. Knee: heel elevation.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.cue: Step directly back and lower the back knee toward the floor — front knee does not travel past the toes and torso stays upright.
exercises.rationale: Safer than forward lunge as deceleration forces are reduced — the preferred lunge for knee and low back clients and all corrective phase work.
exercises.notes: Best lunge variation for knee protocol clients.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.cue: Drive through the heel of the working leg only — do not push off the back foot, and the working glute should be loaded the entire movement.
exercises.rationale: Trains single leg strength and balance in a controlled range — box height determines difficulty and can be adjusted for any fitness level.
exercises.notes: Foot/Ankle: low box only, ensure stable landing.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat Progression
exercises.cue: Use TRX or support initially — hinge at hip of standing leg, extend opposite leg forward, lower under full control to full depth.
exercises.rationale: The highest single leg squat progression — builds extreme unilateral strength, mobility, and balance simultaneously.
exercises.notes: Not for Elder, knee, or low back clients.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift — Dumbbell
exercises.cue: Push hips directly back toward the wall behind you, maintain flat back throughout, feel hamstrings load before returning — moment back rounds the set is over.
exercises.rationale: Teaches the hip hinge pattern under safe load — the most important movement pattern for posterior chain development and low back protection.
exercises.notes: Entry hinge for all avatars. Low back: reduce range before rounding.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift — Barbell
exercises.cue: Same as DB version but bar stays close to legs throughout — drag it up the thighs on the way back up and keep lats engaged to prevent bar drift.
exercises.rationale: Barbell RDL allows heavier loading of the hip hinge pattern — primary posterior chain developer for intermediate and advanced programs.
exercises.notes: Elder: stay with DB version unless very stable.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.cue: Stand centered, push floor away rather than pulling bar up, lock hips out fully at top with glute squeeze — do not hyperextend lumbar at lockout.
exercises.rationale: Reduces spinal shear versus conventional deadlift while allowing maximum loading — the best deadlift variation for general population and low back clients.
exercises.notes: Best primary hinge for most clients. Universal recommendation.

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.cue: Set lats before pulling, brace 360 degrees before bar leaves floor, drive floor away and keep bar against legs throughout.
exercises.rationale: The foundational strength movement — highest systemic demand of any exercise and the most muscle mass recruited in a single movement.
exercises.notes: Elder contraindicated. Low back: only with excellent mechanics.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.cue: Wide stance, toes out 45 degrees, grip inside the legs — push knees out hard and think about spreading the floor apart as you drive up.
exercises.rationale: Reduced range of motion and more upright torso than conventional — excellent for Architect avatar and clients with hip mobility advantages.
exercises.notes: Architect primary hinge variation. Emphasizes glutes and adductors.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust — Barbell
exercises.cue: Upper back on bench, bar across hip crease with pad, drive through full foot and squeeze glutes hard at the top — hold one second at lockout every rep.
exercises.rationale: The highest glute activation exercise available — directly targets the gluteus maximus through full hip extension and is non-negotiable for Architect protocol.
exercises.notes: Architect primary movement. All avatars benefit. Apex: load heavy.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust — Dumbbell
exercises.cue: Same as barbell version — DB sits across hip crease, drive through full foot, squeeze glutes at top for a full second.
exercises.rationale: Entry point for the hip thrust pattern — accessible for all fitness levels and the correct regression before barbell loading.
exercises.notes: Best entry for Elder and Restoration protocols.

exercises.name: Good Morning
exercises.cue: Bar on upper traps, hinge at hip with soft knee bend until back is parallel to floor — spine stays neutral throughout, no rounding.
exercises.rationale: Builds posterior chain strength under extreme hip hinge demand — develops the spinal erectors and hamstrings that support the conventional deadlift.
exercises.notes: Advanced only. Low back and Elder contraindicated.

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL — DB
exercises.cue: Hinge from hip of standing leg, back leg rises as counterbalance — keep hips level and do not let non-working hip rotate open.
exercises.rationale: Combines hip hinge mechanics with single leg balance and hip stability — exposes asymmetries and builds the unilateral posterior chain strength that protects the knee.
exercises.notes: Bodyweight first for Elder and corrective phase.

exercises.name: Single Leg Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Same setup as bilateral, one leg extended — drive through working heel only and keep hips level, do not allow working hip to drop.
exercises.rationale: Maximizes unilateral glute loading through full hip extension — essential for Architect protocol and addressing glute asymmetry.
exercises.notes: Non-negotiable for Architect specialization day.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.cue: Face away from cable, hinge back between legs to stretch hamstrings, drive hips forward to stand — squeeze glutes at lockout.
exercises.rationale: Teaches hip hinge with continuous cable tension — excellent for clients who cannot feel their glutes in deadlift patterns and all corrective phase clients.
exercises.notes: Best hinge teaching tool. Use early in all programs.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.cue: Hike the bell back between legs with hip hinge, then explosively drive hips forward — the arms float up from hip power, not a shoulder raise.
exercises.rationale: Trains explosive hip extension and posterior chain power — combines strength, conditioning, and power development in a single movement.
exercises.notes: Elder: use light KB and master pattern first. Low back: hip hinge must be clean.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.cue: Lower dumbbells with elbows at 45 degrees from body — not flared, not tucked — press up and slightly together at the top.
exercises.rationale: Builds horizontal pressing strength with independent arm loading that corrects bilateral asymmetry and is safer for the shoulder than barbell pressing.
exercises.notes: Shoulder mod: reduce range of motion. Use neutral grip if impingement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Press
exercises.cue: Set bench 30–45 degrees, press up and slightly together — incline angle reduces shoulder impingement risk versus flat pressing.
exercises.rationale: Upper chest development with reduced shoulder stress — the recommended pressing variation for shoulder protocol clients and all corrective phase work.
exercises.notes: Best entry pressing variation for shoulder issues.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.cue: Retract scapulae before lowering bar, touch chest with control, drive feet into floor as you press — bar path should arc slightly back over the eyes.
exercises.rationale: Maximum horizontal pressing load — the primary upper body strength exercise for advanced programming.
exercises.notes: Shoulder flag: do not use. Elder contraindicated.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.cue: Press the bar up and forward in its natural arc — keep core braced throughout and do not let lower back arch as the weight moves.
exercises.rationale: The most shoulder-friendly pressing variation — arc of motion follows natural shoulder mechanics and completely avoids impingement position.
exercises.notes: Go-to pressing variation for shoulder protocol clients.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.cue: Full body tension from head to heel, lower chest to within one inch of floor, fully extend arms at top — no sagging hips.
exercises.rationale: The most honest upper body strength test — requires relative strength and full body tension simultaneously.
exercises.notes: Regression: incline push-up. Progression: weighted vest or archer push-up.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
exercises.cue: Slight forward lean, slight elbow bend throughout — feel the stretch at the bottom and squeeze at the center, do not let the weight pull you back.
exercises.rationale: Isolates the pectoral muscle through full range of motion — builds chest fullness that compound pressing cannot achieve alone.
exercises.notes: Shoulder mod: reduce range, keep elbows higher.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.cue: Press straight up with a slight arc inward at the top — ribs stay down and core stays braced, do not hyperextend lumbar to assist the press.
exercises.rationale: Vertical pressing strength and overhead stability — requires full shoulder mobility and is a key movement for athletic performance.
exercises.notes: Shoulder flag: do not use. Architect and Elder: landmine press instead.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.cue: Start with palms facing you, rotate to palms forward as you press — full rotation happens in the bottom half of the movement.
exercises.rationale: Trains shoulder through a greater rotational range than standard overhead press — excellent for shoulder health and deltoid development.
exercises.notes: Shoulder caution: only if full ROM is available without pain.

exercises.name: Landmine Push Press
exercises.cue: Use a slight leg drive to initiate the press — arc of the bar follows the landmine track, core braced throughout.
exercises.rationale: Introduces power development into pressing — the leg drive teaches force transfer from lower to upper body in a shoulder-safe arc.
exercises.notes: Best vertical press progression for shoulder clients.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.cue: Drive elbows back past hips, squeeze shoulder blades at end of every rep — torso stays still, all movement from arms and upper back.
exercises.rationale: Builds horizontal pulling strength and scapular retraction in a supported position — eliminates lumbar demand and is safe for all avatars.
exercises.notes: Best entry row for all avatars. Shoulder mod: neutral grip attachment.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
exercises.cue: Lie prone on incline bench, let arms hang fully at bottom to stretch lats, row to hip level — retract shoulder blades at the top.
exercises.rationale: Completely eliminates lumbar demand — the safest rowing variation for low back clients and the best way to isolate upper back without compensation.
exercises.notes: Primary row for all low back clients. No lumbar demand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row — Single Arm
exercises.cue: Brace on bench with opposite arm, row dumbbell to hip level — elbow stays close to body and shoulder blade retracts fully at the top.
exercises.rationale: Unilateral rowing exposes side-to-side strength asymmetry and allows heavier loading per side versus bilateral variations.
exercises.notes: Shoulder: neutral grip DB, do not pull above hip level.

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.cue: Hinge to 45–60 degrees, brace before each rep, row bar to lower sternum — maintain hinge position throughout without standing up.
exercises.rationale: Heavy horizontal loading with high posterior chain demand — develops serious back thickness and strength.
exercises.notes: Low back and Elder contraindicated. Use chest-supported version instead.

exercises.name: TRX Row
exercises.cue: Body angle determines difficulty — feet forward increases load, keep body straight from head to heel and retract scapulae at the top.
exercises.rationale: Scalable horizontal row requiring zero equipment beyond TRX — excellent for all fitness levels and joint-friendly for shoulder protocol clients.
exercises.notes: Most accessible row variation. Angle determines difficulty.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Lean back slightly, pull bar to upper chest with elbows driving down and back — do not round forward or use momentum.
exercises.rationale: Builds vertical pulling strength and lat development in a controlled position — the correct starting point before pull-up progressions.
exercises.notes: Shoulder mod: use neutral grip attachment. Do not pull behind neck.

exercises.name: Neutral Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Same mechanics as standard pulldown — neutral grip reduces shoulder rotation demand and is the recommended variation for shoulder protocol clients.
exercises.rationale: Neutral grip eliminates shoulder impingement risk in the pulldown — the primary vertical pull for shoulder clients.
exercises.notes: Go-to vertical pull for shoulder protocol.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Dead hang at bottom, drive elbows down and back to pull chest to bar — do not kip or swing.
exercises.rationale: The highest relative strength vertical pull — requires and builds serious back and arm strength simultaneously.
exercises.notes: Regression: lat pulldown or banded pull-up. Elder: lat pulldown only.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.cue: Supinated grip, dead hang at bottom, pull chin over bar — supination increases bicep involvement versus pull-up.
exercises.rationale: Supinated grip increases bicep contribution — easier than pull-up for most clients and builds arm size alongside back strength.
exercises.notes: Often easier than pull-up. Good stepping stone.

exercises.name: Cable Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.cue: Arms straight throughout — pull bar from overhead to thighs by driving elbows down, focus on feeling lats contract at the bottom.
exercises.rationale: Isolates the lats without bicep involvement — excellent for developing the mind-muscle connection with the lats.
exercises.notes: Shoulder: keep range within comfortable limit.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.cue: Pull directly to face with elbows finishing high and wide — pause one full second at maximum external rotation before returning.
exercises.rationale: Directly combats the internal rotation dominance from pressing and daily life — mandatory for shoulder health in all programs.
exercises.notes: Should appear in every program. Non-negotiable shoulder health exercise.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Slight forward lean, lead with elbows not wrists — raise to shoulder height only, do not shrug at the top.
exercises.rationale: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width development — the primary isolation exercise for deltoid aesthetics.
exercises.notes: Shoulder caution: pain-free range only. Use cable for constant tension.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly
exercises.cue: Hinge forward, arms hang with slight elbow bend — raise to shoulder height by squeezing rear delts and retracting shoulder blades.
exercises.rationale: Targets posterior deltoid and rotator cuff stabilizers — directly addresses the postural deficits common in desk workers and former athletes.
exercises.notes: Essential for posture correction. Pairs well with face pulls.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.cue: Arms straight, lead with pinkies to externally rotate — squeeze shoulder blades at end range of every rep.
exercises.rationale: Activates posterior shoulder stabilizers before pressing — the single most important shoulder warm-up exercise.
exercises.notes: Warm-up and accessory. Include in shoulder protocol.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: Press lower back completely flat into floor before moving — lower opposite arm and leg simultaneously, stop before back lifts.
exercises.rationale: Trains anterior core bracing in a deloaded position — the foundational core exercise that directly transfers to spinal stability under every loaded movement.
exercises.notes: Core staple for all programs. Progression: add dumbbell pullover.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Brace like you are about to take a punch, press out to full extension and hold two seconds — resist every inch of rotation.
exercises.rationale: Trains anti-rotation stability — the ability to resist rotational forces protects the lumbar spine in all asymmetrical movements.
exercises.notes: Non-negotiable core exercise for all avatars and programs.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.cue: Full body tension from head to heel, push floor away with forearms, squeeze glutes — a plank is a full body exercise not just shoulders and abs.
exercises.rationale: Isometric anterior core endurance — builds the sustained bracing ability needed throughout every loaded session.
exercises.notes: Progression: shoulder tap, body saw, weighted plank.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.cue: Straight line from head to feet, drive hip up away from floor — do not let the hip sag or rotate forward.
exercises.rationale: Trains lateral core stability and hip abductor endurance — directly supports knee and low back health.
exercises.notes: Essential for knee and low back protocol clients.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.cue: Hold weight at one side and resist every urge to lean toward it — torso stays completely vertical and shoulder stays packed.
exercises.rationale: Trains lateral core stability under a loaded walking pattern — directly transfers to real-world unilateral loading demands.
exercises.notes: Shoulder: keep loaded arm locked, no overhead reaching.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.cue: Start from knees, brace hard before rolling out — roll only as far as you can maintain a flat back, pause and return with control.
exercises.rationale: The highest difficulty anti-extension core exercise — requires and builds extreme anterior core strength and shoulder stability.
exercises.notes: Low back and Elder: master plank first. Progress gradually.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.cue: Arms slightly bent, rotate the bar from hip to hip using your core — hips and feet stay square, do not rotate the lower body.
exercises.rationale: Trains rotational power and anti-rotation stability simultaneously — directly transfers to athletic performance and sport-specific movement.
exercises.notes: Athletic programs primarily. Low back: limit range.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.cue: Top leg on bench, bottom leg hanging — lift hip off floor and hold straight line, do not let pelvis rotate forward.
exercises.rationale: The most demanding lateral core and hip adductor exercise — builds extreme lateral stability that supports knee health and athletic performance.
exercises.notes: Elder and knee contraindicated. Advanced programs only.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: Stand tall, shoulders back and down, core braced — walk with controlled steps and do not let shoulders creep toward ears.
exercises.rationale: Builds grip strength, core stability, and postural endurance simultaneously — the most transferable loaded carry for daily life and metabolic conditioning.
exercises.notes: Finisher and Slot E staple. Shoulder: keep arms straight down.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry
exercises.cue: Lock arm overhead with elbow straight and shoulder packed — wrist stays over shoulder the entire carry.
exercises.rationale: Demands extreme shoulder stability and core anti-rotation under a walking pattern — directly transfers to overhead athletic performance.
exercises.notes: Shoulder flag: do not use. Elder contraindicated.

exercises.name: Bear Hug Carry
exercises.cue: Hug the implement tight to your chest, elbows in — walk with control and maintain upright posture.
exercises.rationale: Loads the anterior core and upper back simultaneously — the most accessible carry for clients who cannot grip or have shoulder restrictions.
exercises.notes: Best carry for shoulder clients. Easy to scale.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.cue: Quarter squat, swing arms and jump — land softly with bent knees on the box, step down, never jump down.
exercises.rationale: Develops explosive lower body power and rate of force development — teaches full hip extension in a jumping context.
exercises.notes: Knee and Elder contraindicated. Apex and Operator athletic day only.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.cue: Quarter squat and drive hips back, then explosively extend hips — land softly with bent knees and absorb through the legs.
exercises.rationale: Horizontal power development — directly transfers to acceleration mechanics and first-step explosiveness for former athletes.
exercises.notes: Apex primary power exercise. Phantom athletic day.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Jump
exercises.cue: Moderate load, quarter squat, then explosively drive up and leave the floor — land with soft knees.
exercises.rationale: Loaded jump with trap bar — the safest way to develop power under load with minimal spinal stress.
exercises.notes: Apex primary power movement. Advanced athletes only.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.cue: Raise ball overhead, brace core, and slam into floor with full force — catch or pick up and repeat immediately.
exercises.rationale: Total body power expression — trains force production from the ground up and provides a high-intensity finisher option for all fitness levels.
exercises.notes: Low back mod: reduce overhead reach. Shoulder mod: keep arms lower.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
exercises.cue: Rotate from hips not spine — load into the back hip, then explosively rotate and throw into wall.
exercises.rationale: Develops rotational power that transfers directly to athletic performance in all sport movements.
exercises.notes: Athletic programs primarily. Low back: limit range of motion.

exercises.name: 500 Meter Row
exercises.cue: Full drive through legs first then lean back and pull — maintain consistent stroke rate and output throughout.
exercises.rationale: Full body cardiovascular demand with joint-friendly loading — the primary cardiorespiratory assessment tool and high-quality finisher for all programs.
exercises.notes: Track time every session. Beat it next session.

exercises.name: Row Intervals
exercises.cue: 40 seconds max effort, 20 seconds complete rest — maintain consistent output across all intervals.
exercises.rationale: High-output aerobic intervals with measurable progress — distance per interval tracked and beaten session to session.
exercises.notes: Score = total distance. Beat it next session.

exercises.name: Bike Intervals
exercises.cue: 40 seconds max effort, 20 seconds rest — keep RPM consistent across all intervals.
exercises.rationale: Zero impact cardiovascular conditioning — the best finisher option for knee and foot/ankle clients.
exercises.notes: Best finisher for knee and ankle clients. Score = total calories.

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.cue: Low athletic position, drive through balls of feet — maintain constant pressure and do not stand upright.
exercises.rationale: Maximum lower body metabolic demand with zero eccentric loading — cannot cause soreness, safe for all injury profiles, and brutally effective.
exercises.notes: Elder: light load. Knee: no knee flexion past 90. Score = distance.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry Intervals
exercises.cue: Carry for 40 seconds at pace, set down and rest 20 seconds — maintain upright posture throughout.
exercises.rationale: Grip, core, and postural endurance finisher — builds work capacity while reinforcing posture under fatigue.
exercises.notes: Score = total distance. Accessible for all avatars.

exercises.name: KB Complex
exercises.cue: Swing into clean into press into front squat — do not put the bell down until the prescribed reps are complete.
exercises.rationale: Multi-movement KB complex that hits the entire body in minimal time — maximum metabolic demand in minimum time.
exercises.notes: Intermediate and above only. Multiple flags: use row intervals instead.

exercises.name: Battle Ropes
exercises.cue: Alternate arms with full extension — maintain athletic stance and breathe continuously.
exercises.rationale: Upper body dominant metabolic finisher — zero lower body impact and excellent for clients with lower body restrictions.
exercises.notes: Score = work sets completed. Shoulder caution: keep arms lower.
